completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented the online-discovery -> Zotero+PDF -> ingest bridge: a new zotero-write.sh item-add operation (wrapping zot add --pdf) and a new literature-ingest-online.sh entry point with a documented STABLE CONTRACT (directive tokens/exit codes) that classifies discovery records, downloads and magic-byte-verifies PDFs, creates or attaches Zotero items, delegates to the unmodified literature-ingest.sh pipeline, and patches index.json/sub-index metadata. Wired into commands/literature.md Mode A and documented in EXTENSION.md/README.md/a new pattern doc.

memory_candidates.content: When a bash pipeline script's downstream success line is extracted via grep for a doc_id/token, verify the EXACT prefix the upstream script's logger uses (e.g. literature-ingest.sh's log_out() prepends '[ingest] ' to every stdout line). A bare '^Ingested: ' anchor silently fails to match '[ingest] Ingested: ...', and the failure mode is silent: the extraction falls through to a fallback value with no hard error, so a metadata patch keyed on the wrong id becomes a silent no-op rather than a visible bug. Always test doc_id/token extraction against the REAL captured stdout of the delegate script, not an assumed format.

Before binding a mock HTTP server to a well-known local port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:23119 for Zotero's local API) to test a script against a simulated live-API dependency, check whether the real service is already running on this machine. A failed bind (Address already in use) can reveal a genuinely live, real-data-backed instance of the dependency being mocked -- discovered here when a bind attempt to 23119 returned the user's actual Zotero library contents instead of a clean connection-refused. Treat this as a hard stop for further mocking on that port, not just a retry-on-different-port situation, since the risk is touching real user state, not merely a test-infra inconvenience.

A wrapper script that adds a CREATE-item operation alongside several existing MUTATE-existing-item operations (each requiring a mandatory KEY positional argument) needs its argument parser to special-case the new operation's name in the KEY-requirement check, not just add a new case arm in the dispatch -- otherwise the parser will demand a KEY that the create-operation's actual first argument (typically a flag like --pdf) can never satisfy. Grep for how -h/--help are already excluded from a KEY requirement as the template for adding the new exclusion.
